key_insight: METTA proposes memory-enhanced adaptation to help reinforcement learning agents learn new tasks from limited interaction. It targets the trade-off between compressing past experience into a recurrent hidden state and retrieving trajectory history with costly transformers.
problem_solved: Fast adaptation requires retaining useful evidence across long interaction histories. Recurrent agents compress that history into hidden states, while transformer-based agents incur quadratic memory and computation costs.
method: Introduce Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation (METTA) for meta-reinforcement learning.
Use memory-enhanced adaptation to support learning from experience on previously unseen tasks.
Decompose the fast adaptation phase; the supplied abstract is truncated before the components and implementation are described.
impact: This work targets a practical bottleneck for agents that must adapt quickly while using long histories. The supplied excerpt does not establish performance gains or computational savings.
